title: Microsoft Purview: recurring classifier refresh for existing content
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap dates, documented scan controls and qualified endpoint billing statements are supported. Minor corrections should cite the endpoint policy-evaluation source, qualify the classifier-selection statement and align the checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to evolve On-Demand Classification into recurring classification refreshes.
claims.quote: Evolve On-Demand Classification into recurring classification refreshes

claims.claim: The planned refreshes help keep existing content classification current as data and context change.
claims.quote: help keep existing content classification current as data and context change.

claims.claim: Today's on-demand classification is an admin-initiated scan.
claims.quote: On-demand classification runs only when an admin starts a scan.

claims.claim: The wizard lets administrators configure scan scope and location.
claims.quote: Scope and location - You can choose to scan all SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts, only specific ones, or skip certain sites and accounts from the scan. For endpoint devices, you can scope the scan by users.

claims.claim: The wizard lets administrators select classifiers.

claims.quote: Select View estimation. ... After reviewing the estimates, you can edit the scan to narrow or expand the scope. ... Select Start classification.

claims.claim: The roadmap record does not specify refresh frequency.

claims.claim: On-demand classification updates classification results.
claims.quote: On-demand classification updates classification results; matching policies determine any resulting actions.

claims.claim: Updated SharePoint and OneDrive classifications can trigger active policies, including applying or removing sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, updated results can trigger active policies, including policies that apply or remove sensitivity labels.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The recurring refresh's default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview recurring classifier refresh default; Purview recurring classification refresh schedule licensing default. Read the roadmap description and on-demand-classification; neither states what the recurring refresh does on arrival.

claims.claim: No checked source states existing on-demand scans will change or describes a user-facing refresh change.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview recurring classification refresh schedule licensing default; recurring classification refreshes billing roles scope. Opened on-demand-classification and endpoint documentation; the roadmap gives no migration or user-interface behaviour.

claims.claim: Classification scans examine sensitive content in files in scope.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview on-demand classification identifies and classifies sensitive content in historical data stored in SharePoint, OneDrive, and endpoints.

claims.claim: For SharePoint and OneDrive scans, Content Explorer updates within seven days.
claims.quote: Applies to SharePoint and OneDrive ... Content Explorer updates within seven days of scanning to reflect newly classified content.

claims.claim: Viewing classification results requires Content Explorer Content Viewer or Content Explorer List Viewer membership.
claims.quote: To view classification results, you must be a member of one of these role groups: ... Content Explorer Content Viewer ... Content Explorer List Viewer

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Running today's scans requires the Compliance Administrator role group.
claims.quote: To run a scan, you must be a member of the following role group: ... Compliance Administrator

claims.claim: The roles for creating or changing recurring refreshes are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview recurring classification refreshes billing roles scope. Opened on-demand-classification, New-SensitiveInformationScan and Set-SensitiveInformationScan; they document today's scans, not recurring refresh roles.

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes can bound SharePoint on-demand scan scope.
claims.quote: Adaptive scopes for SharePoint on-demand classification let administrators define scan scope dynamically based on site attributes

claims.claim: Administrative units support bounded and delegated SharePoint scan administration.
claims.quote: Administrative units (AUs) for SharePoint on-demand classification let organizations scope and manage scans within defined administrative boundaries, enabling delegated administration

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Scanned files are evaluated against DLP, Information Protection, Data Lifecycle Management and Insider Risk Management policies.
claims.quote: Files are evaluated against DLP, Microsoft Information Protection (MIP), data lifecycle management (DLM), and insider risk management (IRM) policies simultaneously.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/on-demand-classification-endpoints to sources and cite it for endpoint policy evaluation; the already-cited on-demand-classification page gives this statement under SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether recurring refreshes retain estimation and manual review.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview recurring classification refresh schedule licensing default; recurring classification refreshes billing roles scope. Opened on-demand-classification and endpoint scan documentation; only today's estimate and start workflow is described.

claims.claim: Selecting specific classifiers updates only their results, so other classifiers' policies might not trigger.
claims.quote: Applies to SharePoint and OneDrive ... If you select specific classifiers during a scan, only those classifiers have their classification results updated for the scanned files.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'For SharePoint and OneDrive, choosing specific classifiers updates results only for those classifiers, so other classifiers' policies may not trigger.'

claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive location in several active scans is processed by only one and skipped by the others.
claims.quote: If a location is in scope of multiple active scans, only one scan processes it successfully and marks it skipped for others.

claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive scan can process up to 150,000 locations.
claims.quote: Applies to SharePoint and OneDrive ... Each scan can process up to 150,000 locations and 100 million files.

claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive scan can process up to 100 million files.
claims.quote: Each scan can process up to 150,000 locations and 100 million files.

claims.claim: EDM scans rescan previously classified files, potentially increasing cost.
claims.quote: Tenants using EDM classifiers should be aware that On-Demand Classification scans (including estimation and classification) rescan previously classified files, which can increase overall scan costs.

claims.claim: The on-demand classification page names no single licence and instead links to enterprise plans and service descriptions.
claims.quote: For information on licensing, see ... Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans ... Microsoft 365 Service Descriptions

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Today's on-demand classification page says billing can be pay-as-you-go, per-user licensing, or both.
claims.quote: This feature uses pay-as-you-go billing or per-user licensing for Microsoft Purview capabilities or both.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The consumption licensing model and variable cost rating describe the documented on-demand classification meter.
claims.quote: Other Microsoft Purview solutions that use pay-as-you-go pricing ... On-demand classification ... Asset, based on the number classified per scan

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The billing models page meters SharePoint and OneDrive on-demand classification by assets classified per scan.
claims.quote: On-demand classification | Applies when you run a scan to identify and classify sensitive content in data stored in SharePoint and OneDrive | Asset, based on the number classified per scan

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing requires associating the Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview Usage center reports pay-as-you-go usage units.
claims.quote: The Usage center provides detailed information on Total Units Used about your pay-as-you-go billing usage by feature and by workload.

claims.claim: Actual scan billing can be lower than the estimate when items or locations are skipped.
claims.quote: The actual billed amount may be lower than the estimated cost if some items or locations are skipped during the scan.

claims.claim: The usage control is in Microsoft Purview portal > Usage center > Pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: To access the Usage center > Pay-as-you-go and Usage center > Premium usage pages ... The Usage center in the Microsoft Purview portal

claims.where: controls[2]; Cost and licensing: Control; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Usage center can toggle On-Demand Classification between paused and active states.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go usage page also lets you toggle the features listed between paused and active states. ... On-Demand Classification | Yes | Yes

claims.where: controls[2].note; Cost and licensing: Control; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checked documentation does not explain how pausing usage affects a scan already running.
claims.quote: Searched: On-Demand Classification pause active scans PowerShell API usage center; Purview Usage center pause API PowerShell On-Demand Classification. Opened purview-billing-usage and on-demand-classification; neither explains in-progress scan effects.

claims.claim: Endpoint scan estimation is not billed.
claims.quote: Is estimation billed? ... No. Estimation is a metadata-only pass. ... No charges are incurred during estimation.

claims.claim: Eligible previously classified endpoint files with unchanged content and classifiers are neither rescanned nor billed.
claims.quote: Previously classified files, skipped files, and failed files aren't billed. ... When a file has already been classified and neither the file content nor the classifiers have changed, the existing classification result is retained on subsequent scans without rescanning.

claims.claim: Reusing an earlier endpoint classification requires that it used advanced classification.
claims.quote: Reuse of previously classified verdicts requires that the earlier scan used advanced classification.

claims.claim: Recognizing eligible previously classified endpoint files requires the latest Windows cumulative updates.
claims.quote: A file qualifies as previously classified when all the following are true: ... The device has the latest Windows cumulative updates installed.

claims.claim: Endpoint recognition is not retroactive and the first scan after the required update establishes the baseline.
claims.quote: Previously classified file recognition isn't retroactive. It only applies to scans run after the required Windows update version 10.8821 is installed. Scans completed before this update aren't eligible. Your first post-update scan establishes the baseline for all future scans.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Not yet published; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No billing rule or rate specific to recurring refreshes is published in the checked sources.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview recurring classification refreshes billing roles scope; recurring classification refresh schedule licensing default. Opened on-demand-classification, purview-billing-models and endpoints-best-practices; only current scan billing is described.

claims.claim: Create a scan in Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Classifiers > On-demand classification > New scan.

claims.claim: Usage center is in preview.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview Usage center feature is in preview.

claims.claim: A policy being tested can remain in simulation while other active policies act on scanned SharePoint and OneDrive files.

claims.claim: Items for review shows specific items found during the scan.
claims.quote: On the Items for review tab, review specific items found during the scan. You can filter and export the result.

claims.claim: Estimation results include item counts and estimated cost.
claims.quote: On the Estimation overview tab, review scan results, including progress, items found, and estimated cost.

claims.claim: The documented current scan and billing controls are not documented as controls for the planned recurring refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview recurring classification refresh schedule licensing default; on-demand classification schedule recurrence; recurring classification refreshes billing roles scope. Opened current scan, billing and cmdlet references; none describes the roadmap refresh.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to review or keep configured appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: List the active DLP, auto-labeling, retention and Insider Risk Management policies ... Keep policies you are still testing in simulation ... Record which role group members can create scans
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullets beginning 'List the active DLP', 'Keep policies you are still testing in simulation', and 'Record which role group members'. The controls table has no policy-mode or role-membership review control; retain the documented policy and role facts in the explanatory prose.
